memo.verdict: PARK, at medium conviction. Altri does not progress to Early-Stage Assessment on this pass. The memo adopts the risks report's own stage-progression recommendation, that concentrated long-only investors let the Altri investment idea sit rather than progressing to active due diligence, and states that report's reason verbatim: the risk-reward profile remains unfavourable until domestic wood inflation eases and Biotek proves its dissolving pulp price premium. The memo adds a third, independent blocker the risks report does not weight, the entry multiple, with the current price-earnings ratio at the 94th percentile of its own range. Four park reasons are given: the base fails (net debt to trailing EBITDA of 5.5x, return on capital employed of 3% in the first half of 2026, a 2027 refinancing wall); the premium inverted (dissolving pulp at USD 898 per tonne against hardwood pulp at USD 1,409, a 36% discount where the five-year average was a 44% to 47% premium); the entry point (a cyclical bought at a top-decile multiple on trough earnings inverts the setup logic); and the guardrails (six ranked drivers, six live change-from-current items and an eight-item headwind list breach three of the five simplicity guardrails). The memo is explicit that this is not a quality verdict on the asset base, which is energy self-sufficient, cost-advantaged within Europe, and has distributed 124% of market capitalisation since 2017. Watchlist placement is a quarterly review cadence tied to the reporting calendar rather than a fixed date. Six named reassessment criteria are written into Section E and reproduced below. No position is recommended; the memo is a recommendation for Richard's Friday review.
case: The case for the verdict runs in the memo's own order: the change is real, the base is not, and the entry price removes the remaining margin.

First, the change forces are genuine and mostly self-generated, which is why this is a park and not a kill. Element E1 Required Attribute 1 grades C on the strength of the internal leg. Biotek converts fully from paper-grade to dissolving wood pulp by end-2026. The volume proof is already visible: dissolving pulp sales reached 47.5 thousand tonnes in Q2-26, up 92.8% year on year, with more than ten customer qualifications running in Asia and Europe. Caima's bio-based acetic acid and furfural unit started up in June 2026 exactly as guided. Altri holds 58.68% of AeoniQ with a pre-industrial unit due at Caima in the fourth quarter of 2026. The founders moved from co-chief-executive roles to non-executive seats with an external successor. The memo judges the internal programme the higher-quality half of the change equation because it is company-controlled, funded and already producing volume rather than dependent on a benchmark price, and rates Altri's change-force reading above the peer-set median, where Holmen, Lenzing, Elopak and Metsa Board all grade D on this element.

Second, the external leg is two-sided and turning down again. The June 2026 rebound to USD 1,409 per tonne is real, and supply discipline is real: Suzano is idling about 450 thousand tonnes, Canfor closed a 300 thousand tonne softwood mill, Domtar closed a 380 thousand tonne mill, and Bracell dedicated a line to dissolving pulp, removing 600 thousand tonnes of paper-grade supply. Against that, Jefferies notes Chinese hardwood pulp rolled over in July after a 20% rally and industry forecasts point to European gross price declines into the fourth quarter of 2026; Arauco's Sucuriu project adds 3.5 million tonnes by end-2027, lifting its capacity 68%; and a 12% year-on-year dollar depreciation cut first-quarter 2026 revenues with consensus putting the euro-dollar rate at 1.16 by late 2027.
counter_case: The memo carries the counter-case at full strength in four forms and rejects each on stated grounds rather than by assertion.

The strongest single counter, carried at Element E1, is that a 3% return on capital employed is a transitional artefact of front-loaded capital spending, exactly as the chief executive argues, citing a larger asset base ahead of project earnings, and that returning return on capital to historical mid-teens levels is management's primary eighteen-month objective. The memo rejects it because the argument requires the dissolving-pulp premium to return, and that premium is currently a 36% discount rather than the 44% to 47% on which the whole conversion was underwritten.
triggers: Six reassessment criteria, as written in Section E. One, net debt to trailing EBITDA below 4.0x, the earnings review's own stated trigger for the year-end 2026 print. Two, the Biotek dissolving-pulp cash-cost premium converging from 25% toward the 10% to 15% steady-state target. Three, the dissolving-to-hardwood pulp spread restored to a premium, against the current 36% discount. Four, the current price-earnings percentile falling below the median of its own ten-year range, from the present 94th percentile. Five, the AeoniQ pre-industrial unit producing at Caima, releasing the EUR 20m held in escrow pending verified operational test results. Six, two consecutive quarters without a sequential wood cost increase above 5%, the change-forces report's own warning threshold.

What would flip the verdict to progress: a de-rating into the bottom quartile combined with a restored dissolving-pulp premium, which would make the trough-on-trough turn the primary setup rather than the secondary one. What would move it toward a kill: any failure to launch the AeoniQ pre-industrial unit in late 2026, which triggers the risks report's own pre-mortem re-evaluation.

Five key questions carried to Early-Stage Assessment. What is the steady-state EBITDA margin of the converted Biotek asset, where the earnings review records analyst estimates dispersed between 18% and 25%. What is the sustainable dividend once leverage is normalised, given EUR 51.3m was distributed in a quarter when net debt rose EUR 49.5m. How much of the 2026 EBITDA recovery is fair-value and insurance driven, given insurance indemnities boosted first-half results and biological assets swung negative EUR 7.3m. What replaces Project Gama as the medium-term volume path now the Galician configuration is archived. What is the true wood self-sufficiency figure, where the digest carries both a 15% to 20% statement and an over-20% statement for 2025.

Monitoring set. Weekly Chinese pulp pricing indexes and consumer inventory accumulation, named leading warning indicators for a price rollover. Quarterly biological asset fair-value volatility, a multi-channel warning flagging both wood cost inflation and forest productivity decline. The reported annual carbon permit deficit, tracking both fossil-fuel dependency and emissions-scheme benchmark reductions. The least-monitored risk is local wood procurement micro-pricing, which remains highly opaque due to extreme land fragmentation, so cost shocks arrive without warning. Domestic wood procurement share against the 60% to 70% level management cited for the second quarter of 2026.

Research gaps recorded for the next stage. No leadership-foundations report exists on disk, so operator quality is un-evidenced ahead of Element E9. The peer channel needs Navigator ratings and four peer master digests backfilled before the next cohort-relative grading pass can be struck on narrative rather than composites. Reassessment timing is the third-quarter 2026 release, with the fourth-quarter print carrying the 4.0x leverage test.

Recorded conflicts a later reader must not re-derive. Return on capital employed: the risks report states 6% for the first half of 2026 while the change-forces and earnings-review reports both state 3%, and the business-foundations digest states 6% for FY25; the memo uses 3% for the first half of 2026 and 6% for FY25. Through-cycle return on capital: both 16.3% for 2017 to 2025 and a mid-teens average of 15% appear; the memo uses 16.3%. FY25 profit: net profit of EUR 21.4m against a proposed full distribution of about EUR 34m, unresolved in source, likely attributable versus total group. Dissolving pulp capacity: a combined 300 thousand tonnes in the earnings review against 185,000 tonnes in the business-foundations digest; the memo prefers the higher figure on arithmetic. Variable-rate debt: 54% in the annual report against 61% in Q2-26. Wood self-sufficiency: 15% to 20% against over 20%. Dissolving pulp price: USD 898 per tonne in July 2026, with USD 808 and USD 882 per tonne also appearing in the source set.
